trajectory_summary: The call opens cold and administrative, warms through a genuine bill-pain and vulnerability disclosure, then drifts into an extended, disorganized bill-collection stretch complicated by a landline/no-smartphone constraint. The rep secures a tentative appointment but closes with unresolved financial questions answered in specific (scope-creep) terms and a customer-volunteered scam anecdote left unaddressed.
outcome_dispute: The appointment is tentative, not firmly booked: the rep says 'we'll go ahead and set a tentative appointment' (13:44) and the confirmation channel is uncertain — the rep promises a callback/text via cell but the primary contact is a landline, and the customer's closing scam story (16:54-18:54) is left without a direct reassurance tying the follow-up call to legitimacy. Given the comp model is paid-on-sits, this appointment is at meaningful risk of not holding.

observed_outcome.quote: We'll go ahead and set a tentative appointment for next Saturday at 2PM.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day and time (Saturday the 18th, 2PM) were agreed, but the rep's own language labels it tentative, and no co-owner exists to confirm (customer confirmed she is sole owner at 03:00).

bill_anchor_audit.flip_quote: Oh, I'm so sorry that it's so high. We can definitely help you lower that electric bill, with solar energy.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captures the $621 figure and immediately ties it to the solar pitch as the reason to act, satisfying the ask-acknowledge-flip pattern even though the subsequent kWh/dollar data collection becomes disorganized.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: The electric bill going higher and higher.
interest_reason_audit.use_quote: We can definitely help you lower that electric bill, with solar energy.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep asked the interest question early and used the stated reason (rising bills) directly in the immediate pitch, tying the bill pain to the solar offer.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Setter scope discipline on financial questions
primary_coaching_focus.quote: how much do I have to put down?
primary_coaching_focus.why: Two consecutive direct financial questions (14:46 and 15:57) were answered with specific program and guarantee language instead of being bridged to the specialist — this is the clearest repeatable pattern on the call and the easiest to correct with a single reusable line.

key_moments.quote: It's hard for me to get around. I have a sclerotic nerve problem.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep responds with 'Oh, I'm I'm so sorry to hear that' (05:15) — an acknowledgment, but doesn't bridge to how solar specifically helps this situation before moving straight back to bill logistics.

key_moments.quote: That that lost me my job, and so now I'm living off of Social Security, which is not a whole lot. So I gotta make every penny count these days.
key_moments.stewart_read: A second, deeper vulnerability disclosure (fixed income, job loss) immediately follows the first; rep moves directly into 'Okay. So what which one we're looking at?' — pure task redirection with no acknowledgment at all.

key_moments.quote: I said, no. I pay them every month. The one time they did that, I went, called the main office. I had three months without any electric because they messed it up.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer vents a billing dispute with the utility company itself — not an objection to Ion's offer, so objection_inversion's cost/time/interest trigger doesn't apply. This is bill-pain material the rep could have anchored ('that's exactly the kind of unreliability solar gets you away from') but instead simply says 'Okay' and moves to booking.

key_moments.quote: how much do I have to put down?
key_moments.stewart_read: A direct financial question that belongs to the closer; rep answers fully ('Nothing down... you qualify for the program that will install solar at no cost to you') instead of using the escape hatch.
